sections.h2: Who sends the bill and who collects it
sections.html:
Two offices share the work in Allen County. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) appraises every parcel. The Allen County Sheriff collects the money. The PVA doesn't set your tax and can't take a payment. Your bill is the assessed value multiplied by rates set by the county government, the school board and special districts such as the library and health department.

Allen County offices that touch a property tax bill
OfficeAddressPhone
Property Valuation Administrator201 W Main St #1, Scottsville, KY 42164(270) 237-3711
Sheriff, tax collector194 W Wood St, Scottsville, KY 42164(270) 237-3210
Sheriff, owners who never got a billScottsville(270) 237-3388

The PVA is open weekdays until 4:30 in the afternoon. The sheriff's page on the county website has a tax bill search, and the PVA's page posts the certified tax roll and ownership information for anyone to check.

Kentucky values property and fixes ownership as of January 1. If you buy a house later in the year, that year's bill still goes to the prior owner, although the PVA tries to mail the new owner a copy using the recorded deed. A buyer who gets nothing in the mail should call the sheriff's office.

The calendar comes from KRS 134.015. Pay the full bill on or before November 1 and 2 percent comes off. Through December the printed amount applies. In January a 5 percent penalty is added, and from February the penalty is 10 percent.

The sheriff keeps collecting until April 15. At the end of that day every bill still unpaid goes to the county clerk and is recorded as a lien against the parcel, which is then called a certificate of delinquency. A tax sale can't be held sooner than 90 days after that and must happen within 135 days. In between, the county attorney mails notices and the clerk advertises the list a month or more ahead of the sale date.

Once the account is with the clerk, interest runs at 1 percent a month, and the clerk and the county attorney add commissions. The state's worked example starts with a $1,000 bill and shows it costing $1,387.79 if paid within five business days of the transfer, $1,611.30 after the county attorney's first notice, and $1,704.21 when an outside buyer pays at the tax sale. Those figures rest on assumed rates, so a real payoff will differ a little.

Start with the PVA. The state requires a conference with the PVA or a deputy before an appeal is accepted. The real property roll is open for viewing for 13 days beginning the first Monday of May, and the PVA announces the dates in the newspaper with the largest circulation.

After the conference, file with the county clerk no later than the workday after viewing ends. A panel of local property owners hears the case, between 25 and 35 days after viewing ends. Bring condition photos, repair estimates, insurance records and nearby sales. Evidence counts only when it is presented with you and the PVA's representative both in the room, and any change in value has to come with a written explanation.

You may record the hearing on audio. If bills are printed while your case is pending, they use the value you gave on the form. If the board lands on a higher number, a supplemental bill covers the difference, so give an honest figure.

sections.h2: What a typical Allen County house carries
sections.html:
Kentucky's state real property rate for 2025 is 10.6 cents on each $100 of assessed value, down from 10.9 cents in 2024. Local levies sit on top of that, and the sheriff's tax bill search shows the full amount for any parcel. The county's midpoint home value is $192,300, so most owners fall near that range.

The 2 percent early-payment discount applies to the whole bill, not only the state share.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption for seniors and disabled owners
sections.html:
Owners at least 65 years old, and owners with a total disability classification, can claim the homestead exemption. The deduction is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, and it comes off assessed value before the rates are applied.

It is not automatic. Send the application to the Allen County PVA at (270) 237-3711. Disability-based claims need yearly renewal. Two groups skip that step: veterans with a service-connected disability, and owners found permanently and totally disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

An overdue bill leaves a lien that stays with the land. The statute keeps it alive until it is paid or eleven years run out, whoever holds title, so a buyer's title company will find it and ask that it be cleared. A seller who owes money should pay it or have it paid from the sale price.

  1. Ask the Allen County Sheriff for a written payoff, and ask for it close to the closing date so the figure is firm.
  2. If the bill already went to the clerk after April 15, get the payoff from the clerk instead, since interest and commissions are now running.
  3. Have the closing agent pay the balance from your proceeds and record the release.
  4. Give the buyer's mailing address for next year's bill.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and repair requests, but the tax lien still has to be paid at closing, so the same steps apply.

Allen County touches Tennessee, and Scottsville is the seat and only city. The 2020 census counted 20,588 residents, and the latest federal estimate for July 2025 is 22,536, a rise of 9.5 percent. There were 9,390 housing units in 2025, with 74.5 percent owner-occupied. Only 17 building permits were issued in 2025, so most sales are resales of existing houses. US 231, a four-lane parkway, links Scottsville to Interstate 65 about 30 miles away.

A fire at the courthouse in 1902 destroyed some county records, which can make very old title research harder. A seller with a clean deed of record and a paid-up tax account usually faces fewer questions at closing.

faqs.q: Which Allen County office takes tax payments?
faqs.a: The sheriff does, under KRS 134.140 and 160.500. The office at 194 W Wood St in Scottsville answers at (270) 237-3210. The PVA's role ends with valuation.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Allen County taxes late?
faqs.a: Late payment costs 5 percent more in January and 10 percent more afterward. Once the bill reaches the clerk after April 15, interest of 1 percent a month, commissions and fees join in.

faqs.q: Is the Allen County homestead exemption automatic at age 65?
faqs.a: No, you have to apply at the Allen County PVA. The amount is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, and you must be 65 or over, or totally disabled.

faqs.q: I bought a house in Allen County after January 1. Who gets the tax bill?
faqs.a: The seller's name appears on that year's bill, because ownership for tax purposes is fixed as of January 1. The PVA tries to mail a copy to the buyer. If nothing comes, call the sheriff.

faqs.q: Can an Allen County tax lien block a sale?
faqs.a: It can slow one down. The lien stays on the parcel until the debt is paid or eleven years pass under KRS 134.420, and a change of owner doesn't remove it. Get a payoff from the sheriff and clear it at or before closing.
